competitors.description: All five engines stitched into one monster: exact templates, keyword rules and the neural parser at their high gates, then medium keyword/neural/fuzzy recall, with Adapt low as the last resort.
competitors.notes: The kitchen-sink fusion — every arena engine in one pipeline, precision stages before recall stages.

competitors.description: Nebulento × Adapt fusion — precise keyword rules take the first shot, fuzzy matching mops up typos and ASR noise, and Adapt medium catches the remainder.
competitors.notes: Demonstration fusion: keyword precision first, fuzzy recall second.

competitors.description: Padatious × Nebulento fusion — the neural parser leads at high confidence, fuzzy string matching mops up typos and ASR noise, neural medium catches the rest.
competitors.notes: Neural-first template cascade with a fuzzy middle stage for noisy input.

competitors.description: Padatious × Adapt fusion — the intent-classifier stages of the stock OVOS pipeline in shipped order: Padatious high, Adapt high, then Adapt medium. First stage whose own confidence gate fires wins.
competitors.notes: Mirrors the default mycroft.conf intents.pipeline restricted to arena-supported engines (m2v stage omitted until it joins the roster).

competitors.description: Padacioso × Padatious fusion — deterministic regex templates take the exact matches, the neural parser sweeps up paraphrases the templates miss.
competitors.notes: Precision-first template cascade: exact match high, neural medium fallback.

competitors.description: Adapt × Palavreado fusion — the keyword family closes ranks: both rule engines at their high gates first, then both again at medium.
competitors.notes: All-keyword cascade; useful as the keyword league's pooled upper bound.

competitors.description: Classic rule-based keyword intent parser from the Mycroft era: intents are built from required and optional vocabulary groups, matched by keyword presence regardless of word order.
competitors.notes: Single-stage pipeline at the plugin's own medium-confidence gate; per-plugin config keeps the shipped defaults.

competitors.description: Keyword-rule intent engine in the Adapt lineage, rebuilt for OVOS with better multilingual tokenisation. Intents are vocabulary-group rules; matching is order-independent keyword presence.
competitors.notes: Single-stage pipeline at the plugin's own medium-confidence gate; per-plugin config keeps the shipped defaults.

competitors.description: Two-stage hierarchical k-NN over a pre-built FAISS IVF+PQ index of IBM Granite multilingual embeddings: domain-level search scoped to loaded skills, then intent-level scoring with Wu-Lin pairwise probability estimation.
competitors.model: IBM Granite Embedding 97M Multilingual R2 (quint8 ONNX) + FAISS index
competitors.notes: Single-stage pipeline at the plugin's own medium-confidence gate; per-plugin config keeps the shipped defaults. Published predictions are migrated from the legacy ovos-intent-benchmark, where this engine was trained on the benchmark's own corpora; the pinned pretrained model targets real OVOS skill intents and cannot emit this benchmark's label space, so native re-sweeps require a dataset-trained variant.

competitors.description: Scikit-learn text classification behind the OVOS pipeline API: any sklearn featurizer plus classifier can be wired in, with probability calibration applied automatically. The default baseline is a calibrated linear SVM.
competitors.notes: Single-stage pipeline at the plugin's own medium-confidence gate; the per-plugin config pins the documented linear_svc baseline (TF-IDF word featurizer + CalibratedClassifierCV-wrapped LinearSVC), slot tagging and confidence thresholds.

competitors.description: Trains one SVM per intent over one-hot keyword vectors, selecting the most relevant negative samples by fuzzy token-set ratio. Entities come from simplematch templates and wordlists.
competitors.notes: Single-stage pipeline at the plugin's own medium-confidence gate; the per-plugin config pins the documented confidence thresholds. The engine itself is fixed: one SVM per intent over one-hot keyword vectors.

competitors.description: Classifies utterances with a pretrained Model2Vec static-embedding intent classifier restricted to intents registered by loaded skills. The default model is multilingual, distilled from LaBSE.
competitors.notes: Single-stage pipeline at the plugin's own medium-confidence gate; per-plugin config keeps the shipped defaults. Published predictions are migrated from the legacy ovos-intent-benchmark, where this engine was trained on the benchmark's own corpora; the pinned pretrained model targets real OVOS skill intents and cannot emit this benchmark's label space, so native re-sweeps require a dataset-trained variant.

competitors.description: Trains one word-level Markov chain per intent from example utterances and picks the intent whose chain yields the lowest perplexity; confidence is derived from perplexity. Trains in milliseconds with no GPU.
competitors.model: order-2 word-level Markov chains, Kneser-Ney smoothing with backoff
competitors.notes: Single-stage pipeline at the plugin's own medium-confidence gate; the per-plugin config pins the documented model parameters (n-gram order, smoothing, backoff, stemming, char fallback) and confidence thresholds.

competitors.description: Fuzzy-matching intent engine: compares utterances against example sentences with string-similarity ratios instead of exact rules, trading precision for resilience to typos and ASR noise.
competitors.notes: Single-stage pipeline at the plugin's own medium-confidence gate; per-plugin config keeps the shipped defaults.

competitors.description: Deterministic, regex-based drop-in replacement for Padatious. No training step and no false positives on unseen phrasings — what you template is exactly what you match.
competitors.notes: Single-stage pipeline at the plugin's own medium-confidence gate; per-plugin config keeps the shipped defaults.

competitors.description: Lightweight neural intent parser trained on expanded example sentences. The OVOS default intent engine: fast to train, fast to match, tolerant to small variations in phrasing.
competitors.notes: Single-stage pipeline at the plugin's own medium-confidence gate; per-plugin config keeps the shipped defaults.

competitors.description: OpenAI Whisper large-v3-turbo running through the HuggingFace transformers library; a multilingual encoder-decoder speech transformer. Any Whisper checkpoint or local path can be substituted.
competitors.notes: Plugin default model; CUDA optional via 'use_cuda'. Langs pinned to the language set actually exercised in scoring (Whisper is auto-detect/multilingual by design, but an empty langs list made this fighter eligible against every board rather than only the ones it was evaluated on).

competitors.description: Whisper decoding fused with a KenLM n-gram language model via whisper-lm-transformers. This fighter pairs a Basque fine-tuned Whisper medium checkpoint with the HiTZ Basque 5-gram LM.
competitors.notes: README reference configuration; lm_alpha/lm_beta are the published optimized values for Basque.

competitors.description: OpenAI Whisper base model running on whisper.cpp, a dependency-free C/C++ inference engine optimized for CPU (AVX, Arm Neon, mixed F16/F32).
competitors.notes: Plugin default model; ggml weights auto-downloaded on first load. Langs pinned to the language set actually exercised in scoring (Whisper is auto-detect/multilingual by design, but an empty langs list made this fighter eligible against every board rather than only the ones it was evaluated on).

competitors.description: OpenAI Whisper small model running on whisper.cpp, a dependency-free C/C++ inference engine optimized for CPU (AVX, Arm Neon, mixed F16/F32).

competitors.description: Wraps AhoTTS from the Aholab group, a concatenative synthesizer with linguistic processing for Basque and Spanish.

competitors.description: Synthesizes through the Azure Cognitive Services speech service. This fighter runs the en-US-JennyNeural voice from the Azure neural voice catalog.

competitors.description: Renders letters, digits and punctuation as R2D2-style droid beeps by concatenating bundled sound files. Produces signalling sounds rather than speech.

competitors.description: Coqui TTS running the English VITS model trained on LJSpeech, an end-to-end neural synthesizer combining a variational autoencoder with adversarial training.
competitors.notes: Pretrained model id from the plugin README model list; sibling entry points cover XTTS, FreeVC and Fairseq MMS variants.

competitors.description: Unit-selection synthesizer for Galician (also usable for Spanish) that concatenates prerecorded segments, selecting among parallel intonation contours. The default sabela voice balances quality and speed.

competitors.description: Uses the Microsoft Edge read-aloud service via the edge-tts library; no account required. The full Edge neural voice catalog, including multilingual voices, is selectable by voice name.

competitors.description: Wraps the espeak-ng command-line synthesizer, a compact formant-synthesis engine covering over 100 languages and accents. This fighter runs the f1 female voice variant on US English.
competitors.notes: Voice-variant fighter complementing espeakng-m1: same engine and language, female variant appended to the language code (en-us+f1). Requires the espeak-ng binary on the system.

competitors.description: Wraps the espeak-ng command-line synthesizer, a compact formant-synthesis engine covering over 100 languages and accents. This fighter runs the m1 male voice variant on US English.

competitors.description: The Google Translate read-aloud voice via the gTTS library; no account required. The British English accent is selected with the co.uk top-level domain.

competitors.description: Synthesizes through the undocumented Google Translate speech endpoint via gTTS, pinned to the US English accent via the tld option.

competitors.description: LuxTTS, a lightweight zipvoice-based voice-cloning TTS (>150x realtime). Clones the voice in the reference clip pointed at by prompt_audio.
competitors.notes: Voice-cloning fighter — set prompt_audio to a reference clip; a different reference voice is a different competitor. TTS ranks by human votes only.

competitors.description: Client for a MaryTTS server (or MaryTTS-compatible APIs such as OpenTTS and Larynx); the server synthesizes with hidden semi-Markov model and unit-selection voices.

competitors.description: Synthesizes through the Amazon Polly cloud service via boto3, with the Polly voice catalog selectable by voice name and engine tier.
competitors.notes: Requires AWS credentials (key_id/secret_key); plugin defaults shown.

competitors.description: Software Automatic Mouth, a rule-based formant synthesizer producing retro 8-bit robotic English speech. Voice presets are pitch/throat/mouth/speed parameter sets fed to the sam binary.
competitors.notes: Compiles and installs the sam binary on first run when not found system-wide.

competitors.description: The classic energy/denoise VAD extracted from the old ovos-listener: speech is audio whose max/current energy ratio falls below a threshold. No model, CPU-only.
competitors.notes: Energy-based VAD; the ratio/energy thresholds are config. A different threshold is a different competitor on the false-accept / false-reject curve.

competitors.description: Energy/denoise VAD at a higher max/current ratio threshold (3.0) — calls more audio speech than the 2.0 default (lower false-reject, higher false-accept).
competitors.notes: Threshold variant of noise-vad — a different ratio threshold is a different competitor.

competitors.description: A tiny recurrent (precise-lite) TFLite VAD trained with precise-lite-trainer on a mix of wake-word and non-wake-word audio (Common Voice, ESC-50, UrbanSound8K, FSD50K, AudioSet, and community wake-word data), run at its plugin default threshold.
competitors.notes: Baseline at the plugin's default threshold (0.35). The flat key is read by the listener's VAD manager and the nested key is read by the plugin itself, matching the other VAD fighters' key-duplication convention. A -thr03/-thr07-style threshold variant can follow once this baseline is on a board.

competitors.description: Silero neural voice-activity detector running on a small ONNX model; the listener's default VAD. Robust to music and environmental noise.
competitors.notes: Single VAD fighter at the plugin's own threshold; speech decision is 'any voiced frame in the clip'.

competitors.description: Silero VAD at a sensitive 0.3 threshold — calls more audio speech (lower false-reject, higher false-accept) than the 0.5 default.
competitors.notes: Threshold variant: a different threshold is a different competitor on the false-accept / false-reject curve.

competitors.description: Silero VAD at a strict 0.7 threshold — calls less audio speech (lower false-accept, higher false-reject) than the 0.5 default.
competitors.notes: Threshold variant: a different threshold is a different competitor on the false-accept / false-reject curve.

competitors.description: The classic WebRTC energy/GMM voice-activity detector. Tiny, CPU-only and fast; aggressiveness 0-3 trades false-accepts against false-rejects (3 = most aggressive at rejecting non-speech).
competitors.notes: Single VAD fighter; vad_mode pins the aggressiveness. A different vad_mode is a different competitor.

competitors.description: WebRTC VAD at aggressiveness 1 — less aggressive at rejecting non-speech than mode 3 (lower false-reject, higher false-accept).
competitors.notes: Config variant: a different aggressiveness (vad_mode) is a different competitor on the false-accept / false-reject curve.

competitors.description: microWakeWord streaming TFLite model for 'hey jarvis' (the tiny inception-style network used on ESP32 devices), auto-downloaded from the official ESPHome model repository.
competitors.notes: ESPHome publishes models for a fixed phrase set (okay_nabu, hey_jarvis, alexa, …); 'hey mycroft' is not among them.

competitors.description: microWakeWord 'hey jarvis' fronted by a Silero pre-wake VAD gate: the detector only runs on clips the VAD calls speech.
competitors.notes: Combo fighter: wake-word engine + pre-wake VAD. The same engine without the VAD, or with a different VAD, is a different competitor.

competitors.display_name: microWakeWord + Silero VAD + speaker verifier (hey jarvis)
competitors.description: The full listener stack for 'hey jarvis' on microWakeWord: a Silero pre-wake VAD gate, then the microWakeWord detector, then a speaker-verification confirm.
competitors.notes: Combo fighter: pre-wake VAD + wake-word engine + verifier. Each distinct (engine, VAD, verifier) triple is its own competitor.

competitors.description: microWakeWord 'hey jarvis' followed by a speaker-verification gate: an activation only counts when the verifier confirms it.
competitors.notes: Combo fighter: wake-word engine + verifier. The same engine without the verifier is a different competitor.

competitors.description: microWakeWord streaming TFLite model for 'hey jarvis' (the tiny inception-style network used on ESP32 devices), auto-downloaded from the official ESPHome model repository.
competitors.notes: Threshold variant of microwakeword-hey-jarvis: probability_cutoff raised from the plugin default 0.5 to 0.7, trading recall for fewer false activations. Same ESPHome hey_jarvis.tflite model.
Pretrained openWakeWord 'alexa' model.

competitors.description: openWakeWord running its pretrained 'hey jarvis' model on a shared mel-spectrogram + embedding frontend; streams 80 ms frames and scores each against the activation threshold.
competitors.notes: Pretrained model auto-selected by hotword name.

competitors.description: openWakeWord models running on a shared mel-spectrogram and embedding frontend. The pretrained model matching the hotword name is loaded automatically, here the bundled hey_mycroft model.
competitors.notes: Pretrained model auto-selected by hotword name; threshold is the plugin default.

competitors.description: openWakeWord 'hey mycroft' fronted by a Silero pre-wake VAD gate: the detector only runs on clips the VAD calls speech, suppressing false-accepts on music and noise at the risk of missing very quiet speech.
competitors.notes: Combo fighter: wake-word engine + pre-wake VAD. The same engine without the VAD, or with a different VAD, is a different competitor.

competitors.notes: Combo fighter: pre-wake VAD + wake-word engine + verifier. Each distinct (engine, VAD, verifier) triple is its own competitor.

competitors.description: openWakeWord 'hey mycroft' followed by a speaker-verification gate: an activation only counts when the verifier confirms it, trading a small false-reject increase for fewer false-accepts.
competitors.notes: Combo fighter: wake-word engine + verifier. The same engine without the verifier is a different competitor.

competitors.description: openWakeWord 'hey mycroft' at a sensitive 0.3 activation threshold — more activations (lower false-reject, higher false-accept) than the 0.5 default.
competitors.notes: Threshold variant: a different threshold is a different competitor — it lands a different point on the false-accept / false-reject curve and battles as its own entry.

competitors.description: openWakeWord 'hey mycroft' at a strict 0.7 activation threshold — fewer activations (lower false-accept, higher false-reject) than the 0.5 default.

competitors.description: wakewordlab pretrained 'hey jarvis' model on a shared mel/embedding frontend with an optional Silero VAD pre-filter; models are auto-downloaded by name and cached.

The VAD gate (config.hotwords.hey_jarvis.vad / vad_threshold) is built into the plugin's own config block, not a separate listener.VAD pipeline stage — do not expect a listener.VAD block when diffing this against the openWakeWord -silero combo fighters.
